The tag-chip interaction feels natural, but when I start typing I want suggestions from tags I’ve already used, so I can reuse them consistently instead of accidentally creating near-duplicates.

Keeping all ordinary search words as required matches is the right default, and search should stay within the current All, To read, or Reference view. Clicking a tag should also keep me in the current view and add that tag as a filter rather than silently jumping to All. A text search and a tag filter should work together.

The search itself needs a little more depth before I’d lock it in:

- It should ignore capitalization and search the title, description, web address, and any personal note I add to a bookmark.
- Typing `#database` should specifically search that tag.
- Quotation marks should find an exact phrase.
- I want to combine searches with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses—for example, `rome (#article OR #book)`. Plain multiple words can continue to behave like AND.
- If I actually want to search for a word such as “OR,” putting it in quotation marks should treat it as ordinary text.

The current simple search is a good starting point, but I’d like those cases included because they’re what will make rediscovery dependable once the library grows.
